mechanism_narrative: Persistent WORKPLACES deficit (-17.7% at t-0w) signals continued remote work adoption. This suppresses commuter-adjacent retail visits, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has remained between -17.3% and -24.3% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its t-0w level (-23.1%) in three or more of the next four weeks, or WORKPLACES recovers to within -10% of baseline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized near -23.6% (t-0w), indicating a floor in public transport usage. This floor constrains retail access for transit-dependent populations, maintaining downward pressure on RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -20% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has declined from -28.7% (t-3w) to -23.6% (t-0w), showing partial recovery but sustained deficit
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -15% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week despite TRANSIT remaining below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized at -32.0% (t-0w), suggesting outdoor recreation constraints persist. When outdoor alternatives are suppressed, consumers redirect discretionary spending to indoor retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -30% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS has remained between -22.1% and -33.1%, with t-0w at -32.0%
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above -20% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility (-14.4% at t-0w) shows relative stability and modest recovery trend from t-1w (-15.6%). This signals consumer confidence in essential-goods access, which spills over to discretionary retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM declines below -16% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not exceed its t-0w level by week 2 of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated at +7.9% (t-0w), indicating sustained home-based activity. When combined with TRANSIT deficit (-23.6%), this signals mobility constraints that suppress retail access, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +7% AND TRANSIT remains below -20%
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has remained between +7.9% and +9.7%; TRANSIT between -23.6% and -28.7%
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below +5% or TRANSIT recovers above -15%, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT deficits together indicate ongoing mobility restrictions or voluntary avoidance. When both remain suppressed, retail footfall is constrained by reduced commuter traffic and transit capacity, keeping RETAIL_REC below baseline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below -15% AND TRANSIT below -22% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:Both WORKPLACES (-17.7%) and TRANSIT (-23.6%) are suppressed at t-0w
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT recovers above threshold within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -15% in the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS deficit (-32.0% at t-0w) combined with GROCERY_PHARM stability (-14.4%) indicates consumers are prioritizing essential trips while avoiding discretionary outdoor activities. This behavioral pattern suppresses retail-and-recreation visits, keeping RETAIL_REC negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -32.0% and GROCERY_PHARM at -14.4% at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above -25% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 4 percentage points relative to the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized at -23.1% for two consecutive weeks (t-1w and t-0w), indicating a floor in mobility suppression. This stabilization signals that further declines are unlikely; modest recovery is probable as behavioral adaptation occurs, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC remains within ±2 percentage points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC was -23.1% at both t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines below -25% in any of the next four weeks, or remains flat (within ±1 percentage point) for three consecutive weeks.
